notes:
Changes since 0.1.0-beta.9.

### Added

- Final Draft (.fdx) import and export in screenplay mode. Import scripts from the screenplay toolbar, Import Documents, or Open from computer, then continue writing in an editable Stela screenplay.
- FDX interchange preserves scene headings, action, character cues, dialogue, parentheticals, transitions, scene numbers, dual dialogue, title-page text, Letter/A4 paper, and bold, italic, and underline formatting. Original Final Draft metadata is retained for export with compatibility notes where Stela cannot edit or display a feature.
- Import review keeps original FDX files unchanged, saves a snapshot before replacing an open script, and supports Undo. Import/export dialogs use Stela's shared typography, theme colors, accessible controls, and compact layouts.
- Stela's wordmark, application icon, favicon, and branded Windows installer replace the previous placeholders.

### Fixed

- Imported scene numbers and inline formatting survive screenplay editing, preview, PDF, FDX export, and agent edits. Title pages with empty or short contact details no longer insert a blank page.
- Long filenames, compatibility notes, and scene-number controls wrap within compact layouts. Import review keeps actions reachable, shows failures clearly, and supports keyboard focus and Escape.
- Typing avoids repeated catalog writes, unnecessary sidebar renders, redundant outline whitespace processing, and repeated document-metric passes.
- The assistant explains when no AI provider is connected instead of inserting placeholder writing.
- The desktop window appears after the first render to avoid the startup flash. Sidebar tabs, article details, File branding, and save-point hover styling are more consistent.

### Compatibility notes

- FDX support is screenplay interchange; Final Draft's production revision tools and exact production pagination are not provided. Review compatibility notes when importing or exporting. Opening exported scripts in Final Draft itself remains a manual compatibility check.
- Beta.7 and later can install published beta updates through Settings → Updates; earlier versions require one manual install. Beta and stable update channels remain separate.
